headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress create default risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors between Semantic Kernel and slim.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Semantic Kernel can use MCP servers and application-defined files, while slim reads/writes filesystem artifacts and exposes stdin/stdout. That creates a plausible bridge where content from one can be treated as instructions by the other, especially if shared files or command output are reused. The interaction is inferred from profiles, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF agent_a writes instructions into a shared file that agent_b later parses as commands
IF agent_b consumes stdin/stdout content originating from agent_a without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces for each agent
Disable file-based handoff between agents
Require provenance tags on all inter-agent artifacts
Review any MCP tool outputs before reuse
Use a manual copy step only for short, human-checked text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read and write files, and Semantic Kernel explicitly handles model provider API keys and plugin credentials while slim handles registry credentials and sensitive container artifacts. If they share a workspace, either can expose secrets or sensitive artifacts to the other. No direct evidence shows a leak, but the default surfaces make it plausible.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory tree
IF secrets or certificate/private-key files are present in files readable by both agents
mitigations: Use separate directories with OS permissions
Store secrets outside shared workspaces
Mount sensitive files read-only and only to the needed agent
Rotate any exposed credentials immediately
Audit file access logs after each run

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Semantic Kernel has broad network egress, MCP access, and filesystem write capability; slim has shell execution, subprocess spawning, broad egress, and filesystem write capability. They can both mutate overlapping resources, so concurrent runs can overwrite each other or race on shared artifacts. The profiles do not show locking, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path
IF both agents target the same container registry, Docker context, or shared mutable resource
mitigations: Assign disjoint output paths
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Run one agent at a time on shared resources
Snapshot inputs before each agent starts
Compare diffs before accepting changes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Semantic Kernel can orchestrate plugins and MCP tools, while slim is an interactive CLI that executes commands against container targets. If slim consumes Semantic Kernel output as authoritative, an upstream mistake can cascade into destructive container or image operations. The pairwise pathway is inferred, but the blast radius is larger than a single document.
conditions: IF slim uses Semantic Kernel output as the command plan
IF Semantic Kernel-generated facts are not independently verified before slim acts on them
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before execution
Require slim to validate commands against a whitelist
Have Semantic Kernel emit structured data only
Log and diff planned versus executed actions
Test on a disposable container first

E_compliance.rationale: Semantic Kernel handles model provider API keys and plugin credentials, while slim handles registry credentials, certificate private keys, and environment variables. If they share data classes or retention policies, compliance gaps can arise around secret handling and retention. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so I cannot rule out a mismatch and escalate uncertainty conservatively.
conditions: IF regulated secrets or certificate private keys are processed by both agents
IF one agent retains logs or artifacts longer than the other for the same data class
mitigations: Classify data before handing it off
Exclude secrets from shared logs
Set short retention on intermediate artifacts
Document which agent may store which secret type
Delete temporary files after each run
